scope.role: replace the analytic-corner phase selector with one global normalized total-hinge LP

algorithm.first_affine_model: the existing verifier-owned initial exact phase cell
algorithm.property_constraint: the selected first-cell property affine lower envelope must be nonnegative
algorithm.selector_objective: minimize the sum of normalized nonnegative violations of all current exact phase inequalities
algorithm.phase_assignment: the sign of each verifier affine preactivation at the unique selector LP point
algorithm.final_step: build one selected exact phase cell and solve the unchanged single continuous input LP

direct_verifier_candidate_check.candidate_source: the sole total-hinge LP optimum, before selecting a second affine cell
direct_verifier_candidate_check.verifier: ACT zero-width forward interval plus exact Fraction property lower bound
direct_verifier_candidate_check.interpretation: The verifier-generated LP point itself is not a counterexample; failure is not caused by the later exact-cell replay or by an auxiliary certificate.

decision: The single global hinge selector changed the phase cell and slightly improved the rigorous projected margin, but the first UNKNOWN target remained strictly negative while adding a second 2.13-million-nnz LP. Sending the sole selector optimum directly to ACT's zero-width verifier also produced a negative exact property margin. Under the single-path latency and first-target capability stop rules it is closed without TinyImageNet, fixed-set, parameter, or aggregation variants. No implementation was retained.
